children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rose on Friday, climbing back up towards a 19-month peak set earlier this week, while arabica coffee prices were slightly lower.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 0.5% to 20.25 cents per lb. The contract had touched a 19-month high of 21.24 cents on Wednesday. It gained 1.6% for the week.
* Dealers said the El Nino weather event had helped propel prices higher.

* "There is little doubt that this climate event, at an exceptional intensity this season, is hitting yields hard across the world: waterlogged cane in Brazil, drought-hit beet in Europe, stalled planting in western India," Deepcore, a physical sugar broker, said in a note.
* United States sugar production was revised down on Friday by the USDA, which also downgraded the European Union's sugar season.
* White sugar
settled up $1.40, or 0.3%, at $542.50 a metric ton. The market logged a weekly gain of 2%.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled up 13 pounds, or 0.3%, at 4,246 pounds per ton. The London cocoa market was flat for the week.
* Dealers said cocoa continued to be weighed by the large global surplus in the 2025/26 season.
* They noted third-quarter grind data next week should provide a short-term focus with Europe and North American reports due to be issued on October 15.
* Brazil's third quarter grind rose 16.4% from last year to 53,743 tons, industry group AIPC said on Friday.
* New York cocoa
​​was little changed at $5,665 a ton. It was also flat for the week.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 2.1 cents, or 0.7%, at $2.8695 per lb​​, a one-week low. The arabica market lost 0.6% in the week.
* Dealers said the strong pace of exports from top producer Brazil was keeping a lid on prices despite concerns that the El Nino weather event will curb global output in the 2027/28 season.

* "There is genuine tension surrounding this topic," said Cazarini Trading Company about El Nino, adding that so far crops are fine in Brazil but the period between late October and mid-January will be crucial.
* Robusta coffee
gained 1.4% to $3,470 a ton.
